searches.query: I bought a final-sale outlet tent 18 months ago. A stitching seam has now separated in normal use; this was not a disclosed outlet flaw. Does final sale prevent a warranty claim, what evidence do I need, and will an approved manufacturing-defect return cost me a label fee?

chunks.text: Outlet and final-sale products  Products marked final sale in the outlet cannot be returned merely because the customer changes their mind, chooses the wrong color, or finds a lower price later. The final-sale marking appears on the product page and the order confirmation. A general store promotion does not make a product final sale unless the product is specifically marked that way.  Final sale does not remove the manufacturing warranty. A defective outlet tent follows the tent warranty assessment process, including proof of purchase and photos. Cosmetic wear that was disclosed on the outlet listing is not a new manufacturing defect. Support must distinguish a disclosed condition from a fault that arose later.  If the delivered outlet product does not match the listing, report that problem within 14 calendar days after delivery. Keep photographs of the product and the packaging. The support team checks the listing and the received item before arranging a remedy. The 14-day mismatch report window is a separate route from the manufacturing warranty.

Tent manufacturing warranty  Tents have a 24-month warranty for manufacturing defects, beginning on the purchase date. A stitching seam that separates during normal use can qualify. The customer must provide proof of purchase and clear photos so the repair team can assess the failure. The warranty team chooses repair or replacement after assessment; support cannot promise a cash refund before that decision.  Damage from animals, sharp objects, storms beyond the tent's rating, ordinary fabric wear, or incorrect storage is outside this warranty. Accidental damage can still be sent for a paid repair assessment. A quotation must be approved before paid repair work starts. The repair-price guide lists the fixed fees that are currently published; some repairs require an individual quote.  Customers should dry a tent before packing it for inspection. Do not include fuel canisters, batteries, food, or personal belongings. An approved manufacturing-defect claim receives a prepaid ground label.

An approved manufacturing-defect claim receives a prepaid ground label. For a paid repair, shipping is included only if the individual quotation says so. Warranty decisions apply to the specific damage inspected. A previous approved claim does not guarantee that a different problem will also be covered.
A manufacturing defect discovered later follows the product's warranty process. The seven-day transport-report window does not shorten a separately applicable manufacturing warranty.

Who pays for a return label  For ordinary domestic change-of-mind returns, the store offers a ground label for USD 7 per parcel. If the customer uses it, USD 7 is deducted from the refund or store credit. A customer may instead arrange and pay for their own suitable carrier. A store label covers one parcel; two parcels require two labels. Membership does not waive this fee.  An approved wrong-item shipment or manufacturing-defect claim receives a prepaid label without the USD 7 deduction. The support team must approve that reason first. A customer selecting a defect reason in the portal is not sufficient proof that the claim has been approved. The hiking boot fit trial is a fit return, so the normal USD 7 label fee applies unless the customer supplies their own shipping.  Use suitable packaging and keep the carrier acceptance receipt. Items containing an undamaged lithium battery must use the eligible ground service.

Reporting delivery damage or the wrong product  Report visible transport damage or a wrong product within seven calendar days after delivery. Keep the outer packaging and photograph the label, packing materials, and affected item. The support team compares those details with the shipment record before approving the claim. If the item is unsafe to use, stop using it while the report is assessed.  An approved wrong-product or delivery-damage return receives a prepaid label. The customer does not pay the ordinary USD 7 change-of-mind label fee for that approved return. The team confirms whether a replacement or another remedy will be provided. A report being opened does not prove replacement inventory exists or establish a delivery date for the replacement.  Damage involving a rechargeable battery follows the separate damaged-battery procedure. Do not put a leaking or swollen battery in an ordinary return parcel even when support is investigating delivery damage. A manufacturing defect discovered later follows the product's warranty process.

Published repair charges  The repair workshop offers a tent pole-section replacement for USD 18 per section and a sleeping-bag zipper-slider replacement for USD 25. These prices cover the named repair work only. Any transport charge is stated in the individual quotation. Other repairs, including a torn tent floor, require a quote after assessment. There is no published flat price for a tent-floor replacement.  A manufacturing fault approved under warranty is handled under the product's warranty terms rather than automatically charged as a paid repair. An accidental tear or wear outside the warranty can still be assessed for paid repair. The workshop tells the customer the scope and price before work begins. The customer must approve the quotation; sending an item for assessment is not approval for an unspecified charge.  Active members receive priority queue handling but pay the same published repair prices. Priority is not a completion guarantee.

The 14-day mismatch report window is a separate route from the manufacturing warranty. Do not describe it as a 14-day change-of-mind return right. Stock for a replacement outlet product is not guaranteed.

An international customer may use the return route if eligible and place a separate new order. Import taxes and international return transport are covered in the international-orders article. Exchange approval does not automatically waive a return-label fee.

answer.answer: Final sale does not prevent a warranty claim; the manufacturing warranty remains in effect for outlet products. Because the tent is 18 months old, it falls within the 24-month warranty period for manufacturing defects, and a stitching seam separating during normal use can qualify. To submit a claim, you must provide proof of purchase and clear photos showing the failure so the repair team can assess it. If your manufacturing-defect claim is approved, you will receive a prepaid ground label and will not be charged a label fee.
